title: Learning the valve trombone and being forced to play it
summary: The beautiful horn lay around until the band called her up on a bandstand; she practiced a year for a concert in South Bay.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Yes. Oh, it was a beautiful valve trombone. It was a rare instrument. It had a very large bell -- in fact, later as I learned how to play it and I showed up on a television show one night, Tyree was on the show. Tyree Glenn. So I took my horn and I laid it up on the organ hoping somebody would ask me to play. And Tyree fell in love with my horn. From then on, I had to guard it because he wanted it real bad. What happened that night was, I had the horn laying up there, but I was singing. And I guess

Tyree and the rest of the musicians got tired of seeing that horn laying up there doing nothing.
So, the band started playing the last number -- the band started playing "Spozin'" and Tyree handed me the horn right on television.
So I had to do something. I picked it up -- I didn't even know what key they were playing in, but I found a couple of notes and I played it.
I had to play it or else. So anyway --
You got your way through it.
Yeah, yeah. And had fund doing it so much so that later, there was a concert out in -- what, South Bay?
Yes, South Bay.
I was just digging through my notes here.
These were some concerts that Rex Stewart was promoting. He lived out there at the time. He lived out in Babylon.
So, I said I'm going to play. I had rehearsed -- I had been practicing. In fact, when

Cliff brought the horn home, Vic Dickenson gave me a mouthpiece. And I used that mouthpiece to practice with.
And Cliff had a friend who was a trumpet player. And I used to go over to his house and he'd teach me what to do -- you know, how to practice, and all that.
And I practiced diligently for about a whole year, and I had a whole repertoire of songs --
Had you already entered your period of retirement by this time?
Uh --
This was around '56.
Yeah, oh yeah. I hadn't entered into the retirement yet.
Before '56.
Yeah, it had to be before '56.
